basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Ab his divisae sunt insulae gentium in regionibus suis unusquisque secundum linguam suam'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Ab his divisae sunt insulae gentium in regionibus suis unusquisque secundum linguam suam et familiam in nationibus suis. « Legamus antiquorum historias, et videbimus omnes pene insulas, et totius orbis littora, terrasque mari vicinas, a Graecis accolis occupatas, qui, ut supra diximus, ab Amano et Tauro montibus omnia maritima loca usque ad oceanum possidere Britannicum. » Dum vero dicitur unusquisque secundum linguam et familiam in nationibus suis, liquido ostenditur quia juxta opinionem vulgatam singuli qui hic commemorantur filii Noe, vel nepotes filiorum Noe, singulas gentes sive cognationes diversarum fecere linguarum. Nam eadem sententia, enumerata quoque stirpe Cham sive Sem, de varietate generationum linguarumque subinfertur.
